title: Statement Regarding the Publication of Reference Rates on Friday, April 3, 2026
summary: The New York Fed issued an operating policy notice announcing that publication of SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR Averages will be suspended on Friday, April 3, 2026 due to expected non-settlement of cleared Treasury repo. Despite SIFMA not recommending a full market closure for Good Friday (coinciding with the March Employment Situation release), repo market participants broadly expect to treat the date as a holiday, eliminating two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates. EFFR and OBFR will continue to publish per the New York Fed's holiday schedule.
key_points: TGCR, BGCR, SOFR, and SOFR Averages/Index will not publish on Friday, April 3, 2026
Settlement of cleared Treasury repo is not scheduled for April 3, eliminating two of three segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates
Repo market participants broadly expect to treat April 3 as a holiday despite no full market closure recommendation from SIFMA
SOFR and related rates will be published on Monday, April 6, 2026, reflecting same-day settling transactions that settle Thursday, April 2 and mature Monday, April 6
EFFR and OBFR will publish on Friday, April 3 per the New York Fed's holiday schedule
The disruption is driven by the coincidence of Good Friday and the March Employment Situation data release
why_it_matters: SOFR serves as the primary reference rate for trillions of dollars in floating-rate instruments, loans, and derivatives. A temporary suspension of its publication, even for a single day, requires market participants to have fallback arrangements and aware of timing mismatches when rates resume. The note also highlights how macro data release scheduling can interact with market infrastructure decisions.
macro_context: The March Employment Situation report release (scheduled for April 3, 2026) is cited as the reason SIFMA did not recommend full market closure, creating the conditions for repo market disruption.
market_structure_context: The notice directly addresses market plumbing: cleared Treasury repo settlement availability determines whether sufficient data exists to calculate SOFR and related rates. The suspension highlights the dependency of reference rate publication on repo market operations and settlement infrastructure.
